title: Weak saturation under Cartesian pushout product
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A monomorphism means a degreewise injective map. Call a class of maps weakly saturated if it contains all isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts in the category of maps. Here a transfinite composition is the composite of a small ordinal-indexed chain which is a colimit of its earlier stages at each nonzero limit ordinal. A retract in the category of maps is given by commutative section and retraction squares whose composite is the identity square. Let $W$ be any weakly saturated class of simplicial maps. For monomorphisms $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $k:K\hookrightarrow L$, let $\theta_{i,k}$ be the canonical map
$$ (A\times L)\amalg_{A\times K}(B\times K)\longrightarrow B\times L. $$
For each fixed monomorphism $k$, the class of monomorphisms $i$ such that $\theta_{i,k}\in W$ is weakly saturated. For each fixed monomorphism $i$, the class of monomorphisms $k$ such that $\theta_{i,k}\in W$ is weakly saturated.
